title: The Kiosk Remembered Her From Last Time
script: A mom at the trampoline park shoved three families out of the safety-waiver line so her son could jump first, announcing they come here every week like that skipped the rules. I was the front-desk teenager stuck holding the line, and the park's insurance is clear: every child completes the harness check, no exceptions, no regulars, no excuses. She argued for ten straight minutes while her son bounced on a trampoline he wasn't cleared for yet. Then the new check-in kiosk, installed after her last two visits ended in a banned account, flagged her photo ID under a completely different kid's name — the front desk had upgraded to facial recognition that spring, specifically because of repeat troublemakers. Security walked over before I said a single word. She tried explaining it was a sibling's account, loudly, to a line of people she had personally cut. The manager didn't blink — banned families don't get sibling accounts. She left empty-handed, past everyone she'd shoved.
